Honestly looked like an accident how Pavs went down. Cody cross checked him coming off the faceoff, he lost balance falling backwards, fell into Stas who was moving forward to get in position to defend a shot and it caused him to go head first to the ice. Honestly didn't look like a 5 minute major or game misconduct from what I saw on the replay. Really hate to see it happen that way, especially to pavs.

I guy going down awkwardly on what's in most cases a standard crosscheck at a faceoff does not warrant "perspective" for what is absolutely an awful penalty call. If every unfortunate incident in hockey became calls like these, players would play the game a lot less physical in fear of being in the box for 5 minutes for doing what are typically standard plays.

You honestly need to go back and watch the play again. The crosscheck was to the check and isn't all that uncommon off a faceoff. Pavs loses his balance stumbling backward into the 2nd Vegas player as he's falling down. The 2nd player is gliding out to get in a defensive position to stop a shot so he's focused on the puck moving out toward the blue line and the player there, not Pavs falling backward into him on his left. The two players bumping causes Pavs to be unable to get himself in a better possition while falling and causes him to land on his head.

Far from a 5-minute major, not even something that should be a 4 minute as it was a freak fall that caused the bleeding. I can see 2 for a cross-check but anything more is just awful knee-jerking from refs who didn't fully see what happened on the play and called it because of how it looked at the end.

It shouldn't be a knee-jerk reaction to what they're seeing after the events occur though. Hockey is a sport of risk, they're dudes with sticks skating on ice using metal blades on their feet. They can talk about it all they want but the fact that they can't look at it again and not call something when they clearly need to look at the situation as a whole causes just plain awful penalty calls like this one.

The contact with the puck is not on the blade of the stick on that play, it's on the lower part of the shaft. Much like how the puck has to be fully over the line for it to be a goal the puck has to be fully over the crossbar on contact for it to be considered hit in with a high stick. Because it was a good goal on the ice and it's impossible to tell if it's fully above the bar or not that's the right call of a good goal.

I implore you to go look at where the puck is hitting the stick in comparison to Cody's shoulders with how he's standing, and the crossbar and come back to tell me it's 100% not a goal because I'm not convinced it's a high stick.

So you're expecting a guy who's looking past what's happening on his left and suddenly seeing a full-sized man falling back into him to not brace himself for a sudden impact but instead catch the guy while he's wearing hockey gloves, holding a stick, and trying to do his job? He's playing hockey dude, he's not focused on how or if the guys going down but that he's in the way and has to get past him to get in position to play defense. 

Is he shoving him out of the way? Yeah because that's how the game works. Is he purposefully slamming a dude who's already in the air going down to the ice? No.

The fact that Eakin got thrown out of this game and was given a 5-minute major is absolutely ridiculous and is one of the worst calls I've seen in a long time as he did something that isn't unusual nor typically dangerous in that situation.

His status after the fact off what would typically be an innocuous crosscheck to the chest off a faceoff shouldn't determine what is and isn't a 5-minute major. I

n pretty much every other case that's 2 minutes at most because it's a cross check but a bunch of freak extra things happened on this play that caused Pavs to get hurt the way he did. That's not Eakin's fault and he should have been given such a severe penalty on what was a normal hockey play/penalty in open ice until all the extra stuff after happened.

Same dude, you really hate to see it.

Honestly, this whole situation ruined this game for me and I'm irrationally angry about the outcome even though I don't root for Vegas. Couldn't even enjoy watching it play out in overtime because San Jose was given the opportunity to get there by that call.

Cody plays an average of 1:09 on the penalty kill per game. Him getting thrown out incorrectly had a part in that as well as San Jose getting 5 minutes to score as many times as they could up a man. That call changed the entire outcome of the game and series.

Edit:
To add to this. Cody is a centerman on the 3rd line for Vegas. He's taken 16 faceoffs shorthanded in this series alone. So not only are you breaking up a line and taking away the playmaking in the center of that line, but you're removing a key part of the Vegas penalty kill that San Jose was able to capitalize on that powerplay; faceoffs.

People are trying to add strawmen to this discussion by saying, "the series shouldn't have gone this long," or, "but what about this game's call or no call." But this discussion is not about those other things that happened. It's about a call that was made on the ice in the spur of the moment that changed the entire direction of a game. Take out what game of the series it was, take out what happened in other games and isolate this call in the context of the game it was played and what occurred in the game because of it. As someone watching the entire game, Vegas had total control at that point and the call turned the whole complexion of the game. That's the issues we're discussing here.

This discussion isn't about whether or not Vegas should have won a game prior. It's about an occurrence that changed the outcome of a game. Take the context of what game it was in the series and isolate the incident and clearly look at it, don't make excuses like "well Vegas should have won earlier in the series." That's making a strawman that takes away from the real discussion of the issue that occurred.


>It didn't change the outcome tho. Series shoulda been over in 6

Please. This could have happened at any time in any game and it would still be a problem. Would it be talked about as loudly and debated so hotly? Probably not. But it still would be pretty strong as it changed the outcome of a game completely. 

You're doing yourself, the fans, and the people involved a complete disservice by brushing this off like it never should have happened.

He's also a centerman on the third line of Vegas which has a major part in both faceoff and penalty kill. The refs to a centerman out of the game who's taken 16 shorthanded faceoffs this series alone. That's an important penalty killer and it breaks up the checking line. You can say "well they should have done this or that after he got thrown out" but the problem was he was thrown out in the first place. It completely changed everything.

This discussion is not about another game or another "bad call" it's about what happened here in this game and the situation that occurred. You're straw-manning and taking away from looking at and discussing what the problem is here by bringing up something irrelevant to what happened in this game.
